text:
**Short answer: a power station of about 1,000 Wh is the safe pick for a full night. The EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic (1,024 Wh) or the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh) both fit.**

**Why 1,000 Wh**
- Blanket wattage varies by source. The Department of Energy figure of about 60 W for a single and 100 W for a double, and Sunbeam's 110 W rating for full-size blankets, come from [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/). At 100 W, a 1,024 Wh unit runs the blanket for about 8 hours.
- [Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket) rates a queen blanket at about 150 W, cycling to roughly 75 W on average. It estimates 11–12 hours from a 1,000 Wh unit.
- [Homepowerfacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/) assumes a much higher 260 W average for a queen blanket. That would call for about 2,600 Wh for 8 hours. This is the most pessimistic estimate in the results, and it's far above the other sources. I'd treat it as a worst case, not the typical draw.
- Small units fall short. A 288 Wh unit runs a 150 W blanket for only about 3–3.5 hours, according to [Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket).

**Picks**
1. **BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh)** is Blackoutwise's [top pick](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket). It runs a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours and weighs 25 lb. It usually sells for roughly $380–$500.
2. **EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic (1,024 Wh)** has an LFP battery rated for 3,000 cycles, 1,800 W output and a 5-year warranty. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy) lists the bundle with a 45W solar panel at $479 (was $598) at Best Buy. TechRadar hasn't tested this model itself. It also says the 45W panel is too small to recharge the battery quickly, and the unit weighs 26.7 lb.
3. **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is the choice if you want two nights. Blackoutwise says it runs the same blanket for about 23 hours.

**Budget option:** The [BLUETTI Elite 30 V2](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night) (288 Wh, $289.99) is what Dealectric recommends for one blanket. It works for a 12 V blanket on low from the car port, or a low-draw setup. Dealectric is the retailer selling it, so weigh that recommendation accordingly. For a 120 V queen blanket on high for 10 hours, Dealectric says you need about 1 kWh, so this unit won't cover that.

**Tips**
- Plug the blanket straight into the station. Don't use extension cords or power strips, and keep the station off the bed ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night), citing Sunbeam's manuals).
- If you also use a CPAP, a 1,024 Wh unit still lasts about 8 hours with both running ([Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket)).
- Don't plan on a space heater. A 1,500 W heater drains a 1 kWh unit in about 35 minutes ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/)).
